item.vignette: A pediatric low-grade glioma cell line carrying a BRAF fusion is exposed to tovorafenib. MAPK-pathway output falls. In separate kinase assays, the same drug inhibits mutant BRAF V600E as well as wild-type BRAF and CRAF.
item.lead_in: Which direct target profile best explains these findings?

options.A: Type II inhibition of RAF kinases including mutant BRAF, wild-type BRAF, and CRAF
options.B: Selective inhibition of MEK1 and MEK2 only
options.C: Selective inhibition of PI3K alpha with mutant p110alpha degradation

item.tested_construct: Type II inhibition of RAF kinases including mutant BRAF, wild-type BRAF, and CRAF
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Tovorafenib is a Type II RAF kinase inhibitor of mutant BRAF V600E, wild-type BRAF, and wild-type CRAF, and it has antitumor activity in models harboring BRAF mutations or a BRAF fusion.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. This target profile directly matches tovorafenib and explains suppression of MAPK signaling in BRAF-driven tumor cells.
distractor_explanations.B: MEK1/2 inhibition acts one level downstream of RAF and does not match the documented direct kinase targets.
distractor_explanations.C: PI3K-alpha inhibition affects a different signaling axis and is not the direct action of tovorafenib.
distractor_explanations.D: ROS1/pan-TRK inhibition describes a different fusion-targeted kinase profile.
distractor_explanations.E: CSF1R inhibition targets macrophage-lineage signaling rather than RAF-driven MAPK activation.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize tovorafenib as a Type II RAF inhibitor targeting mutant BRAF, wild-type BRAF, and CRAF.

item.vignette: H3 K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma cells are exposed to dordaviprone. Mitochondrial stress signaling increases, apoptosis is induced, and histone H3 K27 trimethylation partially recovers. A separate receptor assay shows reduced dopamine D2 signaling.
item.lead_in: Which pair of direct pharmacologic actions best explains this profile?

options.A: Inhibition of mitochondrial ClpP plus dopamine D2 agonism
options.B: Activation of mitochondrial ClpP plus dopamine D2 receptor inhibition
options.C: Inhibition of HIF-2alpha plus dopamine D2 receptor inhibition
options.D: Menin-KMT2A interaction blockade plus dopamine D2 agonism
options.E: Dual inhibition of mutant IDH1 and IDH2

item.tested_construct: Activation of mitochondrial caseinolytic protease P with dopamine D2 receptor inhibition
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Dordaviprone is a protease activator of mitochondrial caseinolytic protease P (ClpP) and also inhibits the dopamine D2 receptor. In H3 K27M-mutant diffuse glioma models it activates an integrated stress response, alters mitochondrial metabolism, induces apoptosis, and can restore H3 K27 trimethylation.

distractor_explanations.A: The ClpP direction is reversed; dordaviprone activates rather than inhibits ClpP, and it inhibits rather than agonizes D2 receptors.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Dordaviprone directly activates mitochondrial ClpP and inhibits dopamine D2 receptors.
distractor_explanations.C: HIF-2alpha inhibition is a distinct oxygen-sensing pathway mechanism and is not the direct target profile of dordaviprone.
distractor_explanations.D: Menin-KMT2A blockade is used in susceptible leukemias and does not explain the mitochondrial stress phenotype in H3 K27M glioma.
distractor_explanations.E: Mutant IDH inhibition lowers 2-hydroxyglutarate and is mechanistically distinct from ClpP activation.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize dordaviprone as a mitochondrial ClpP activator with dopamine D2 receptor inhibitory activity in H3 K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma.

item.vignette: A patient with generalized myasthenia gravis has pathogenic circulating IgG autoantibodies. After treatment with nipocalimab-aahu, total serum IgG and anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody concentrations fall without direct depletion of B lymphocytes.
item.lead_in: Which direct pharmacologic action best explains this effect?

options.A: Blockade of terminal complement component C5
options.C: Binding to the neonatal Fc receptor, reducing IgG recycling

item.tested_construct: Binding to neonatal Fc receptor and reducing circulating IgG
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Nipocalimab-aahu is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), resulting in a reduction of circulating IgG levels, including pathogenic IgG autoantibodies.

distractor_explanations.A: C5 blockade inhibits complement-mediated injury but does not directly accelerate IgG clearance.
distractor_explanations.B: CD20 depletion reduces B-cell populations and antibody production over time but is not the direct mechanism of nipocalimab.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. FcRn binding interferes with IgG salvage/recycling and lowers circulating IgG, including pathogenic autoantibodies.
distractor_explanations.D: IL-6 receptor blockade alters inflammatory signaling but does not directly reduce IgG through FcRn.
distractor_explanations.E: BAFF neutralization affects B-cell survival and maturation rather than directly blocking IgG recycling.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize FcRn blockade as a mechanism for lowering pathogenic circulating IgG without directly depleting B cells.

item.vignette: Hepatocytes are exposed to a double-stranded oligonucleotide therapy used to rebalance hemostasis in hemophilia. Antithrombin protein synthesis falls after the intracellular concentration of antithrombin messenger RNA decreases.
item.lead_in: Which molecular mechanism directly produces this effect?

options.A: CRISPR-mediated deletion of the SERPINC1 gene
options.B: Antisense blockade of factor VIII translation
options.C: Neutralization of tissue factor pathway inhibitor
options.D: RNA interference causing degradation of antithrombin mRNA

item.tested_construct: RNA interference causing degradation of antithrombin messenger RNA
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Fitusiran is a double-stranded small interfering RNA that causes degradation of antithrombin mRNA through RNA interference, thereby reducing plasma antithrombin levels.

distractor_explanations.A: Fitusiran does not edit or delete the SERPINC1 gene; its effect occurs post-transcriptionally.
distractor_explanations.B: The therapy targets antithrombin mRNA rather than factor VIII translation.
distractor_explanations.C: TFPI neutralization is a different rebalancing strategy that acts at the protein level.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Fitusiran uses RNA interference to degrade antithrombin mRNA and reduce antithrombin protein.
distractor_explanations.E: Thrombopoietin-receptor activation increases platelet production and does not target antithrombin expression.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate siRNA-mediated antithrombin suppression by fitusiran from protein-neutralizing and gene-editing hemostatic strategies.

item.vignette: Autologous keratinocyte-containing sheets are prepared from a patient with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. The cells are transduced ex vivo with a replication-incompetent retroviral vector carrying a full-length gene, then applied topically to chronic wounds. Treated tissue begins producing collagen VII and anchoring fibrils.
item.lead_in: Which gene is introduced into the patient-derived cells?
item.tested_construct: Ex vivo retroviral delivery of COL7A1 to restore collagen VII production
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: ZEVASKYN consists of autologous cells transduced ex vivo with a replication-incompetent retroviral vector containing full-length COL7A1, enabling production of functional collagen VII and restoration of anchoring fibrils.

distractor_explanations.A: KRT14 mutations cause a different inherited epidermolysis bullosa phenotype and do not encode collagen VII.
distractor_explanations.B: LAMA3 encodes a laminin subunit involved in junctional epidermolysis bullosa, not collagen VII.
distractor_explanations.C: COL17A1 encodes type XVII collagen rather than type VII collagen.
distractor_explanations.D: ITGB4 encodes integrin beta-4 and is associated with a different basement-membrane adhesion defect.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. COL7A1 encodes collagen VII, the protein deficient in recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa and restored by this ex vivo gene-modified cell product.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa to COL7A1 deficiency and recognize ex vivo COL7A1 gene transfer as the mechanism of prademagene zamikeracel.
